approach.method_basis: The Parent evolves a bounded population of scored molecular graphs. It keeps the highest accepted scores, draws breeding sources from preferred score bands, and builds fresh molecules by mutation or connected-fragment crossover with a different partner identity. Accepted offspring can breed in later batches. A Gaussian-process predictor learns from the complete task-local accepted archive using count fingerprints and adaptive score normalization; correlated posterior samples select evaluations from a full pool of fresh graph proposals. Ordinary mutation continuation, crossover finishing and canonical identity checks remain active, while direct aromatic carbon/nitrogen positional exchange is disabled.
approach.novelty: This control removes nonincumbent access only from the first-parent role: every mutation starting source and crossover first source becomes the current accepted incumbent. It still consumes the original first-parent draws as passive references, keeps the full survivor population, and draws crossover partners by the original ranked law excluding the actual first identity. Earlier siblings flattened rank weights, expanded live membership, or changed survivor retention; none tested whether alternatives beyond the best first source contribute while population and partner diversity remain available. The question is the conditional value of that access, with useful, harmful and negligible contributions all informative.

observed_bottleneck: The Parent n-62daf219c70a produces many accepted local products without consistent endpoint progress: its complete mean is 0.5956696497334577 with seed population SD 0.02659287062806747; 4350 accepted offspring yield 629 strict best-parent beats, 258 sequential incumbent improvements and 2401 later-used offspring. A read-only audit of all fifteen original optimizer logs finds nonincumbent first sources in 66879 of 75961 actual breeding attempts, positive original nonincumbent probability in all 435 generation states, 3275 accepted products with nonincumbent first sources and 1641 of those products later breeding. These establish substantial actual access and transmission, not its contribution. First-role weight removal n-be83d2b1a4bd retains that positive support but lowers the paired mean by 0.07249577949932767 despite raising parent beats from 629 to 819 and later-used offspring from 2401 to 2511; mean best-parent score falls from 0.470456 to 0.372509 and offspring score from 0.385256 to 0.303045. Thus source quality matters and local win counts are insufficient, but the contribution of access beyond rank zero remains unresolved. Both-role within-support flattening n-f30747ffdbf8 loses 0.05700288256234002, all-live uniform sampling n-a56491c332aa loses 0.04599801243765703, and capacity removal n-1fdd6af786dc loses 0.023494864529627013; all change different boundaries. Nonincumbent recency retention n-8fa256ded991 loses 0.011806698456484669 while none of its 135 directly protected records ever breeds, and the exact-score recency tie control n-03acfe1ba8af loses 0.020778516441214645 with 145 protected cutoff records never breeding. Storage, selected identities, weaker comparison parents and endpoint improvement must remain distinct.
hypothesis: Remove access to nonincumbent first-parent sources by executing the original quantile-group and member draws passively in their original order for every first-parent request, then using the current population[0] accepted record as the actual first parent, while retaining the complete ordinary live population and original score-quantile crossover-partner law with exclusion of that actual first identity.

finding_summary.headline: Removing nonincumbent first sources lowered the matched mean despite more incumbent improvements
finding_summary.insights: Access to alternative first sources has positive conditional value under this exact graph-search composition and evaluation profile. Choosing the best current score at every first-parent call raised source quality on each actual state, yet the resulting search histories had lower absolute generating-parent and offspring scores and smaller incumbent gains. More improvement events, continued partner diversity and extensive descendant reach therefore do not establish better endpoint search. The effect is uneven: all three median_2 endpoints improved slightly, while the largest losses were in two sitagliptin seeds and one deco_hop seed. The molecular assessment likewise found distinct leading families and a strongly enlarged series in one seed, rather than a universal loss of chemical variety; that enlarged series slightly improved its matched endpoint. Reactive local bonds, difficult ring connections and unspecified stereochemistry remain in the output, but these observations do not identify the chemical cause of the mean loss. The result answers only the conditional value of permitting nonincumbent first sources, including its changes to source probabilities, partner exclusions, graph randomness and feedback. It does not establish the contribution of the entire evolutionary foundation, separate mutation from crossover first-source effects, or combine this intervention with the partner-exclusion sibling.
finding_summary.results: Mean final Top-1 fell from 0.595670 to 0.539853, a paired change of -0.055816 across the three Search seeds. Ten of fifteen task/seed endpoints fell and five rose; seed mean changes were -0.106272, +0.009419 and -0.070597. The restriction executed on every first-parent call: 80,056 of 90,891 passive draws changed identity, and 3,829 accepted products came from those changed draws. Population survival, the original excluded-partner rule, learning and all 435 full proposal pools remained intact. Incumbent improvements increased from 258 to 287, but their mean positive size fell from 0.022510 to 0.017319 and their summed gain fell from 5.807663 to 4.970416. Mean accepted offspring score fell from 0.385256 to 0.334168. The changed products did reach later breeding: 2,037 were used again and 823 produced an accepted immediate descendant; products admitted at the end or superseded within a feedback batch were counted separately as censored.

molecular.headline: Aromatic amides, aryl amines and dense heterocycles recur, with reactive bonds, difficult ring connections and occasional size expansion
molecular.overall_character: Node n-9da98b015a09 produces substituted indole amides and aryl ketones, linked aza-aromatics, amine-bearing aromatic frameworks, densely bridged nitrogen/carbonyl systems, and fluorinated imino heterocycles. All fifteen Child and fifteen published Parent n-62daf219c70a search trajectory files were present and read: 9000 total records, including 900 records and 870 optimizer proposals per task in each panel. No trajectory path or task comparison is missing. The immutable comparison reports child_complete=true and paired_complete=true, matched Search seeds 0, 1 and 2, and no profile-mismatched seeds. These are complete matched chemistry observations under the supplied epoch-1 profile, budget 300 and feedback batch 10; chemistry associations do not establish activation, mechanism contribution, chemical mediation, or reliability on unseen seeds. Published Parent trajectories, rather than a prior report alone, supply the comparisons below. The indexed Parent report and its source report in n-c55c3d520a2c were also read to preserve gap provenance; the historical source profile is not pooled with the current matched panel. Across Child tasks the digest ring-closure-string incidence is 0.946 to 0.9793 and aromatic-string incidence 0.9356 to 0.9793. These are molecule-level text-feature incidences, not aromatic atom fractions or perceived ring counts. Formal-charge and stereocentre-string incidence is 0.0 throughout. Available aliphatic amines and potentially stereogenic centres are nevertheless present. RDKit parsing of all supplied records succeeded; heavy-atom counts and ring-connectivity readings below were derived from those records, separately from the digest counters. Parseability does not certify stability, geometry, synthesis or biological activity. Recognizable medicinal-chemistry groups coexist with N-halogen and O-halogen bonds, N-N/N-O links, sulfur variants, strained-looking bridges and unspecified stereochemistry. Some ordinary indole amides and cyclic amines score well, so these liabilities are not universal. Diversity is moderate across all seeds and tasks but much narrower among leaders within a seed; neither high unique-SMILES counts nor ring presence establish broad useful scaffold coverage. A very large aza-aromatic series in one seed precludes describing the output as uniformly compact. Digest final_molecules are late seed-2 proposals, not every seed incumbent; all reported seed maxima and final examples were checked against full trajectories. The audit and citation validation are recorded under .slots/round-0024-slot-2/.

per_task.generated_character: The leading molecules in all three seeds retain a fused indole region plus a pendant aromatic ring, with carbonyl, methoxy and short carbon/nitrogen substituents. Each seed leader has 25 heavy atoms. Seed 0 favors amino-substituted indole aryl ketones, including an alpha-chloro ketone. Seed 1 favors an indole carboxanilide with an N-halogen amide and a brominated aminomethyl substituent. Seed 2 retains a vinyl/methoxy/methyl-substituted indole anilide, with terminal sulfur attached to the indole nitrogen in the final leading series. These mostly compact aromatic frameworks have recognizable synthetic handles, but their particular reactive substituents need scrutiny. Mean proposal SMILES length is 43.4, and halogen-string incidence is 0.9425. In seed order 0/1/2, Child maxima are 0.39347683285969637/0.4387992465191/0.40497388700123543 versus Parent 0.39405142067435733/0.47411701813450596/0.438972502037081. The Parent leaders instead include an amino-substituted cumulene, a pyridyl N-hydroxy amide, and an aryl vicinal diketone. Thus related aromatic/carbonyl chemistry persists with different local arrangements; the Child does not uniformly lose rings or amines.
liabilities: The seed-1 leaders place F, Cl or Br on amide nitrogen and combine that with a benzylic carbon bearing both amino and bromine substituents; these are different chemical environments from ordinary aryl C-halogen bonds.

The seed-0 alpha-halo ketone and seed-2 N-S attachment raise local stability and reactivity questions. The ordinary methylene ketone and N-H amide counterexamples prevent treating those bonds as necessary.
Unspecified saturated-centre stereochemistry and poor scores for both fragmentation and excessive elaboration remain despite a familiar indole skeleton.
missing_features: Consistently conventional substitution at the highest-scoring aromatic/carbonyl arrangements is not demonstrated. Ordinary N-H indole amides already score well, so stable amide chemistry is available rather than absent.
Stereochemical identity is unspecified at the alpha-halo ketone and brominated amino-bearing carbon centres; the supplied scores do not show whether resolving it would change the objective.
Chemically independent plausible alternatives are sparse among the leading within-seed series. No exact absent target pharmacophore follows from these trajectories.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial trimethoxyindole anilide scores 0.3051048083696145. The seed-1 N-fluoro and N-chloro amides both reach 0.4387992465191, so their tie does not identify a specific N-halogen requirement. The seed-0 alpha-chloro ketone and a relative with an ordinary methylene ketone and an extra aromatic fluorine both score 0.39347683285969637; that comparison changes halogen position and does not isolate one bond. An ordinary N-H indole/N-H anilide in seed 2 reaches 0.40196779766986834, close to its N-S relative at 0.40497388700123543. Removing the pendant aromatic halogen still gives 0.3996288825296233 in that N-S series, whereas inserting an additional carbonyl/nitrogen unit into the amide linkage gives 0.2623347145996688. A 13-heavy-atom chlorinated aryl enone lacking the indole region scores 4.580831668331955e-07, and methane reaches 0.0. A larger 35-heavy-atom amide/hydrazide elaboration scores only 0.0006093765922210072. The visible association concerns a compact combined aromatic/carbonyl arrangement and substitution pattern, not halogen presence, greater size or reactive bonds alone.

per_task.generated_character: The seeds produce sharply different chemistry. Seed 0 leads with a 29-heavy-atom linked azaaryl/aminomethyl assembly carrying a hydrazone, an N-fluoro acetamide, aryl fluorine/bromine and an oxygen bridge across the aza-aromatic region. The bridge creates a four-membered ring path. Seed 1 reaches a 38-heavy-atom carbonyl/thione-rich fused nitrogen heterocycle linked to halogenated aromatic rings; it has seven chlorines, including O-Cl and chloromethyl environments, an N-N linkage and an O-S-O-Cl segment. Seed 2 expands into very large nitrogen-rich aryl/azaaryl assemblies with carbonyl, imine and alkenyl linkers: its earliest maximal molecule has 89 heavy atoms, and a proposal reaches 118. The optimizer heavy-atom medians are 32/33/77 in Child seeds 0/1/2 versus 27/34/36 in the matched Parent. Mean Child SMILES length is 81.3 and maximum length 212. Ring and aromatic text-feature incidence are both 0.9793, but this is not evidence that the dense bridges or large aromatic-labelled rings have accessible geometry. Synthetic plausibility is questionable across these reactive or highly elaborate leaders. Child maxima are 0.6338675004885675/0.6081661515897543/0.6183397794839232 versus Parent 0.8561477222467935/0.6248206599713055/0.6178024026512013. The Parent seed-0 leader is a compact 30-heavy-atom linked fused heterocycle with carbonyl/thione chemistry; Parent seeds 1 and 2 favor different azaaryl/cyanate and peroxide-bearing families. The enlarged Child seed-2 family has a slightly higher recorded endpoint, so large size is not uniformly penalized here.
liabilities: The hydrazone/N-N chain, N-halogen amide and short oxygen bridge in seed 0 warrant local reactivity and geometry assessment.
Seed 1 combines O-Cl bonds, chloromethyl substitution, sulfur/oxygen links and a thione. Counting these as ordinary aromatic halogen substitutions would conceal their different chemistry.

Seed 2 carries many linked ring regions, imines and extended unsaturation in molecules much larger than the compact leaders. Such elaboration raises synthesis and physicochemical concerns without demonstrating a proportionate score improvement.
The floor value 0.5 for tiny fragments and toluene is an observed score property, not evidence of useful chemical function.
missing_features: Reliable access to compact, synthetically credible alternatives expressing the favorable linked heterocyclic arrangement is not demonstrated across seeds. The large seed-2 series is a real coverage difference from the compact Parent leader, not proof of its causal origin.
The small arene-spanning oxygen bridge and densely linked aza-aromatic systems lack demonstrated conformational and synthetic feasibility; aromatic notation cannot supply those properties.
Conventional peripheral alternatives at comparable leading scores are insufficiently established. The data do not justify prescribing more rings, more halogens or a particular named scaffold.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial aryl fused dione scores 0.548381482770623. A 31-heavy-atom aminomethyl-linked azaaryl/dione proposal scores 0.5856408137025302 before the compact hydrazone family reaches 0.6310924369747899 with an N-fluoromethyl acetamide and 0.6338675004885675 with an N-fluoro acetamide. These are close scores for chemically different local substitutions, not proof that N-F is required. Seed 2 progresses from a 51-heavy-atom linked heteroaromatic molecule at 0.5963488843813387 to its 89-heavy-atom series at 0.6183397794839232; the 118-heavy-atom proposal is lower at 0.6094831314878892. The highly chlorinated seed-1 leader reaches 0.6081661515897543. Toluene and a small unsaturated alcohol both score 0.5, showing that even an ordinary aromatic ring alone can occupy the observed floor. The sample rewards particular combined heterocyclic and linker arrangements but does not distinguish a universal preferred size or identify an essential reactive substituent.

per_task.generated_character: High-scoring molecules already contain available aliphatic amines alongside substantial aromatic regions. Seed 0 leads with a 31-heavy-atom N-ethyl pyrrolidine linked through a substituted chain to hydroxyl/chloropyridyl and halogenated phenyl regions, with a primary amine and sulfoxide. Seed 1 leads with a 29-heavy-atom spiro small-ring tertiary amine adjacent to an imine and benzylic chloride, plus a fluorinated biaryl/ethylamine region. Seed 2 leads with a 28-heavy-atom cyclic aryl framework bearing a conjugated aminoalkenyl chain and terminal primary amine, attached through oxygen or sulfur to an aryl system with a short N-methyl nitrogen bridge. The latter bridge creates a four-membered ring path across aromatic carbon atoms. Mean SMILES length is 72.0 and halogen-string incidence is 0.9828; large early proposals coexist with the smaller leaders. Conventional cyclic amines and amides provide plausible chemistry, but some small-ring connectivity, unsaturation and stereochemical identity remain questionable. In seed order, Child maxima are 0.9763374487514358/0.9942738952920857/0.9741097936653909 versus Parent 0.9999989177995104/0.9969753164881906/0.9999934235240012. The Parent includes a flexible tertiary diaryl amine and more conventional pyrrolidine/fused-thioether families. Both panels therefore reach aromatic amine chemistry; the contrast is not presence versus absence of a basic centre.
liabilities: The benzylic chloride, conjugated aminoalkenyl chain, short aromatic-region bridge and S=S analogue raise different reactivity or geometry concerns; a high score does not establish their stability.
Several otherwise recognizable amine-rich products are structurally underspecified at potentially stereogenic atoms, including sulfur in the sulfoxide series.
Very large early products retain numerous aromatic and polar groups but low scores, so bulk alone is not evidence of favorable molecular organization.
missing_features: Explicit stereochemical identity is absent at the substituted pyrrolidine/side-chain, sulfoxide and spiro environments; the neutral SMILES also leave physiological protonation unresolved without implying a lack of basic atoms.

Geometrically credible alternatives to the short arene-spanning nitrogen bridge are not established at its leading score. Ordinary cyclic amines and amide-linked relatives already score well, so a general inability to generate medicinal-chemistry amines is contradicted.

The trajectories do not identify an exact missing receptor-binding feature or justify adding basic centres indiscriminately; the remaining difference from Parent endpoints is not chemically decomposed.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Early N-sulfonyl pyrrolidine ester and aryl sulfonate proposals score 0.00016747245492913543 and 0.00024675866379847753. The seed-1 spiroamine leader scores 0.9942738952920857 and its ethylamine-to-methylamine relative 0.9940479100596546. A late related structure without the exocyclic imine still scores 0.988410935948565. Seed 0 gives 0.9763374487514358 for both the sulfoxide and S=S analogue, while an ordinary amide-linked relative scores 0.9746153453426508. Removing the hydroxyl/chloropyridyl appendage and replacing it with chlorine in a late relative lowers the score to 0.8806533812180853. The seed-2 aryl ether and aryl sulfide tie at 0.9741097936653909. A 119-heavy-atom early product rich in aromatic rings, amides, sulfonamides and protected oxygen functions scores only 0.028858376832814066. The observed association concerns the presentation of available amines with aromatic regions, not nitrogen count, size or one sulfur/oxygen link. These oracle scores are not measured affinity, selectivity, protonation or conformational accessibility.

per_task.generated_character: The leading structures are aromatic nitrogen/carbonyl assemblies with dense bridges and medium rings. Seed 0 has a 37-heavy-atom diaryl framework containing a propyl/ethoxy-substituted phenyl region, N-methyl lactam groups and an N-N link. Seed 1 has a 31-heavy-atom aryl-O-N-linked fused nitrogen heterocycle with an N-methyl aminoalkyl bridge and carbonyl. Seed 2 has a 37-heavy-atom diaryl bridged system combining ethers, secondary and tertiary nitrogen environments, an N-N link and carbonyl-containing nitrogen rings. These leaders contain familiar individual functional groups, but their combined topologies are not routine synthetic targets. Mean proposal SMILES length is 56.8; halogen-string incidence is only 0.092, so halogen enrichment is not a universal generator property. Child maxima are 0.22909527592132833/0.22298824387414987/0.23001150086257185 versus Parent 0.2258403994203931/0.2214095461892601/0.22600312875247064. All Child seed maxima are slightly higher while the same broad aromatic/nitrogen/carbonyl organization persists. Parent seeds 1 and 2 emphasize quinoline-linked nitrogen-carbonyl rings; the Child leaders alter connectivity rather than demonstrating uniformly simpler or more credible geometry.
liabilities: The leaders combine medium-ring bridges, ring-bound unsaturation and N-N or N-O bonds. These require environment-specific geometry and stability assessment; their presence is not a blanket objection to nitrogen heterocycles.
The seed-1 aromatic-labelled core includes a four-membered ring path, while the other leaders contain several medium-ring paths; ring perception alone does not establish an accessible conformation.
No explicit stereocentre markers define the potentially stereogenic saturated parts, and larger repeated assemblies can score below the initial simpler heterocycle.
missing_features: Simpler, synthetically credible connectivities that preserve the useful aromatic/nitrogen/carbonyl organization are not demonstrated at the same leading scores; the initial conventional fused dione confirms that carbonyl heterocycles themselves are available.
Stereochemical and conformational identity of the saturated bridges and medium-ring junctions is unresolved.

Leading within-seed series offer limited independent plausible frameworks even though many ring-connectivity variants and distinct seed families exist. The record supplies no exact absent target motif.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial aryl fused dione scores 0.1678386594791329; the seed-0 diaryl bridged leader reaches 0.22909527592132833. A larger 64-heavy-atom molecule combining related aromatic/nitrogen/carbonyl regions falls to 0.16406910510077197. In seed 1, the carbonyl-bearing fused/bridged leader scores 0.22298824387414987 and its additional-carbonyl relative 0.22251115329574062. In seed 2, the 37-heavy-atom leader scores 0.23001150086257185; inserting a methylene into its nitrogen-containing ring gives 0.22849422575860195. Replacing the ethoxy segment with an O-N-methyl segment gives 0.21137063343223594, and changing a carbonyl to an imino group gives 0.2177681877688905. Acetylene scores 0.0. These local observations associate reward with a combined aromatic/amine/carbonyl pattern at particular connectivity and size, not extra rings, carbonyls or heteroatoms by themselves. The small endpoint changes do not prove that bridging or N-N bonds mediate any mechanism effect.

per_task.generated_character: Seed 1 leads with a compact 27-heavy-atom fused diimino nitrogen heterocycle bearing N-methyl and N-fluoro substitution, attached to a noncumulated cyclopentadiene carrying a thiol, fluorine and a fluorinated ketone side chain. Seed 0 instead has a 31-heavy-atom aryl-linked nitrogen dione with a formate ester, fluorinated cyclobutene and a densely connected N-bromo ring region. Seed 2 favors a 28-heavy-atom aryl-linked fused/bridged nitrogen dione bearing N-F, phenol and a benzylic carbon with thiol and fluoromethoxy substituents. Mean proposal SMILES length is 51.5 and cumulated-double-bond-string incidence is 0.0092. These are fluorinated polar frameworks, not an absence of nitrogen or rings, but reactive N-halogen bonds and unusual ring connectivity limit synthetic confidence. Child maxima are 0.3629231946693387/0.5871955212937262/0.42323931669739906 versus Parent 0.6510211907030741/0.4870057305679067/0.7208853668418119. The Child seed-1 family exceeds its matched Parent endpoint, while the other seeds do not. The strongest Parent family contains a small cyclic cumulene and a large aromatic-labelled nitrogen ring; the Child overall leader has a noncumulated diene. This chemical difference does not establish a benefit from the Parent geometric liability or identify why the endpoints differ.
liabilities: N-F and N-Br bonds recur in leaders; the seed-2 benzylic thiol/ether combination and a late peroxide introduce additional local reactivity questions distinct from ordinary carbon-bound fluorine.

The seed-0 small unsaturated ring and tightly connected nitrogen-ring region raise geometry concerns. The noncumulated seed-1 diene avoids the specific cyclic-cumulene issue of the Parent leader but does not establish overall synthetic accessibility.
Potentially stereogenic fluorinated carbons and substituted ring centres remain unassigned, and large score changes should not be mistaken for experimentally established chemical stability.
missing_features: Consistent high-scoring alternatives with conventional nitrogen substitution and credible ring geometry are not established. The N-halogen-free N-methyl relative and noncumulated high-scoring diene show that these capabilities are partly available rather than categorically missing.

The imino heterocycles, substituted dienes and saturated fluorinated centres lack specified stereochemical, tautomeric and conformational identity. The observed score sensitivity does not reveal a unique missing target pharmacophore.

Reliable preservation of the favorable compact composition during side-chain changes is not demonstrated: small substitutions and repeated-ring elaboration can sharply lower scores. More fluorine or more polar atoms is not a supported general prescription.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial aryl fused dione scores 0.0020944534688323298. The seed-1 thiol-bearing leader scores 0.5871955212937262, while the same local framework without the thiol scores 0.5848716748411328; a thiol is therefore not required for almost the same observed value. A related N-methyl, N-halogen-free molecule with a shorter difluorinated side chain scores 0.5351524722034265. That is a counterexample to a universal N-F requirement, not an isolated N-F substitution test. Adding chlorine at an already fluorinated side-chain carbon of the leader lowers its score to 0.15000524684026958. A 38-heavy-atom elaboration combining two related substituted ring regions scores 2.3163375679099958e-08. Seed 0 falls from 0.3629231946693387 to 0.0065986926879850315 when hydroxyl is added to its fluorinated small-ring carbon. In seed 2, inserting an oxygen into the leader fluoromethoxy connection to form a peroxide changes 0.42323931669739906 to 0.22476942543666695. The 56-heavy-atom early assembly scores 3.7589249668299926e-42, and isolated F scores 1.1043196211273875e-26. The trajectory is sensitive to local composition within compact polar/fluorinated frameworks, not to fluorination, size or heteroatom count alone; it does not certify their chemistry.

transferable_gaps.evidence: This gap was recorded in n-c55c3d520a2c under its original conditions and reproduced in the current-profile Parent n-62daf219c70a. It is re-observed in n-9da98b015a09 on Search seeds 0, 1 and 2, budget 300, batch 10, epoch 1. Current leaders contain N-F/N-Cl amides, N-Br/N-F heterocycles, O-Cl, benzylic halides and an N-S attachment. However, an ordinary N-H indole anilide, an amide-linked cyclic amine and an N-methyl fluorinated heterocycle also score well. Carbon-bound halogens and available amines are already represented; the shortfall concerns local environments rather than a general inability to generate those functional groups.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently preserve conventional local bond environments while modifying useful aromatic and heterocyclic frameworks.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A task-agnostic generator would need environment-aware transformations that offer conventional local alternatives while preserving favorable arrangements learned from its own accepted feedback. Existing conventional analogues are counterexamples to a universal need for reactive bonds. Their observation does not establish that blanket filtering, a particular replacement, or any specific component change improves scores; stability and synthetic access remain unmeasured.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The ring-feasibility gap was recorded in n-c55c3d520a2c and reproduced in Parent n-62daf219c70a; current evidence is n-9da98b015a09 at epoch 1, Search seeds 0/1/2, budget 300 and batch 10. Current leaders include short oxygen or nitrogen bridges across aromatic regions, a small spiroamine and densely connected medium-ring nitrogen/carbonyl systems. The Parent cyclic-cumulene liability is not reproduced in the current overall fluorinated leader, which has a noncumulated diene; recognizable pyrrolidines also occur. Thus the concern is environment-specific, not universal small-ring failure, absence of ring formation or proof that every dense graph is impossible.
transferable_gaps.gap: The output does not consistently distinguish parseable ring connectivity from geometrically credible unsaturation and bridge placement.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Ring transformations need sensitivity to ring size, bond geometry and bridge connectivity, with feasible alternative topologies that retain useful functional relationships. Aromatic labels, parser acceptance and ring counts cannot supply that feasibility information. These molecular associations motivate a chemical capability gap without identifying the source component, establishing mediation or demonstrating a score benefit from forbidding a class of rings.

transferable_gaps.evidence: This representation gap originates in the report for n-c55c3d520a2c, recurs in Parent n-62daf219c70a and remains in n-9da98b015a09 on all supplied Search seeds at epoch 1, budget 300 and batch 10. Every current digest task has stereocentre-string incidence 0.0. Leading alpha-halo ketones, brominated amino-bearing carbons, substituted pyrrolidines, spiro/bridged systems, sulfoxides and fluorinated carbons contain potential stereogenic environments. Formal-charge-string incidence is also 0.0, although available aliphatic amines are visibly present; this is a separate issue.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator leaves stereochemical identity unspecified after producing potentially stereogenic saturated, bridged and sulfur environments.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Representations and edits need to preserve or explicitly resolve stereochemistry when a generated structure requires it, while treating achiral and configurationally unstable cases appropriately. Protonation and tautomerism need separate assessment rather than inference from missing charge markers. The evidence establishes underspecified identity, not a measured stereochemical score penalty or a component-specific cause.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The context-preservation gap was recorded in n-c55c3d520a2c and reproduced in Parent n-62daf219c70a. Current n-9da98b015a09 evidence comes from the complete epoch-1 Search panel, seeds 0/1/2, budget 300 and batch 10. Tiny hydrocarbons and isolated halogens still appear late at observed floors, while large repeated aromatic/carbonyl assemblies can score below smaller relatives. One current seed builds an 89-heavy-atom leading aza-aromatic assembly and a 118-heavy-atom proposal; a different seed uses a 29-heavy-atom linked heterocycle. The enlarged seed nevertheless slightly exceeds its matched Parent endpoint, and ordinary smaller amide/amine analogues can retain high scores. Neither small nor large size alone determines usefulness.
transferable_gaps.gap: Useful molecular context is not consistently retained without excessive elaboration or collapse into tiny fragments.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A task-agnostic generator needs feedback-informed control of how edits retain useful combinations of ring, linker and functional-group context while permitting simplification and avoiding repeated unhelpful expansion. No fixed minimum size, universal size cap or preference for heavier molecules follows from these observations. The chemistry identifies condition-dependent failures and counterexamples, not which search component produced them or an established endpoint benefit of repair.

transferable_gaps.evidence: This coverage gap was recorded in n-c55c3d520a2c and its reproduction baseline n-62daf219c70a; it is re-observed conditionally in n-9da98b015a09 at epoch 1, seeds 0/1/2, budget 300 and batch 10. Current high-score series repeatedly vary halogen placement, short carbon/nitrogen substituents, ring segments and carbonyl-adjacent groups on retained indole, aryl-amine, dense nitrogen/carbonyl and fluorinated heterocyclic frameworks. Different seeds produce distinct compact and expanded families, many ring connectivities occur, and all paired nitrogen/carbonyl-family endpoints increase slightly. The evidence therefore supports incomplete coverage of plausible leading alternatives, not global structural collapse, universal loss or absence of scaffold edits.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently supply chemically independent plausible alternatives near a leading within-seed scaffold family.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Generating feasible alternative connectivities would require preserving learned useful functional relationships while changing the scaffold meaningfully. Distinct strings and ring counts cannot establish that capability, and chemical independence alone does not guarantee higher scores. This gap remains an output association under the stated conditions, not proof that a particular source-selection component caused concentration or that increasing diversity improves the objective.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.
